standard.title: Interpret line graphs
standard.description: Interpret line graphs representing change over time; discuss the relationships that are represented and conclusions that can be made
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can acquire and represent data in frequency tables and charts (AC9M5ST01). They have not yet interpreted line graphs as representations of change over time.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret line graphs representing change over time and discuss the relationships and conclusions they represent.

nodes.label: Reading line graphs
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can read values from a line graph and describe what the axes represent.
nodes.minimum_width: Read specific values from a line graph; identify what each axis represents including units.
nodes.typical_width: Read and compare values at specific time points; identify the maximum, minimum and any missing values; describe the overall trend in a sentence.
wider: Compare two line graphs with different scales for the same data
Read line graphs from real media: weather, finance, sport
success_criteria: Student reads specific values from a line graph accurately
Student correctly identifies axis labels and units

nodes.label: Interpreting change and relationships
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the pattern of change shown in a line graph and identify the relationship between the variables.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe whether values are increasing, decreasing or staying the same over a given time period; identify the steepest and flattest sections.
nodes.typical_width: Describe the full pattern of change in a line graph using precise temporal language; interpret what steep and flat sections mean in context; discuss the relationship between the variables.
wider: Compare line graphs for related datasets (e.g. two cities' temperatures over a year)
Investigate line graphs used in First Nations environmental monitoring

response_modes.reason: Slope interpretation requires understanding that steepness = rate of change, not magnitude. Multiple contexts — temperature, population, finance — help students generalise the interpretation principle.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Multi-dataset comparison and environmental monitoring contexts give advancing students rich, purposeful interpretation tasks.
success_criteria: Student describes the pattern of change in a line graph using temporal language
Student interprets what the steepest/flattest section means in context

nodes.label: Drawing conclusions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make and justify conclusions from a line graph, distinguishing between what the data shows and what might explain it.
nodes.minimum_width: Make one conclusion supported by the graph; explain the data evidence for the conclusion.
nodes.typical_width: Make multiple conclusions from a line graph; distinguish between what the data directly shows and possible explanations; discuss limitations of conclusions from a single graph.
wider: Critically evaluate conclusions made in media reports about line graph data
Investigate how the choice of time scale affects conclusions drawn from the same data

response_modes.reason: Data-to-conclusion reasoning varies greatly by context. Students need diverse real datasets to develop genuine reasoning rather than template conclusions.

success_criteria: Student makes a conclusion supported by specific graph evidence
Student distinguishes between what the data shows and a possible explanation
